'''Irene Georgakoudi''' (born 7 June 1971) is a Greek biophysicist and Professor of [[Biomedical engineering|Biomedical Engineering]] at [[Tufts University]], where her work focuses on developing non-invasive [[medical imaging]] techniques based on [[optical spectroscopy]] for applications in medical diagnostics and therapeutics.

== Early life and education ==
Georgakoudi was born in [[Thessaloniki]], Greece.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|last=Georgakoudi|first=Irene|url=https://www.urmc.rochester.edu/MediaLibraries/URMCMedia/labs/foster-lab/documents/georgakoudi-thesis.pdf|title=PhD Thesis: Effects of photosensitizer bleaching and localization on photodynamic oxygen consumption and dosimetry|publisher=[[University of Rochester]]|year=1999|isbn=|location=|pages=iii-iv}}</ref> She moved to the United States in 1989, obtaining a [[magna cum laude]] Bachelor's degree in [[physics]] at [[Dartmouth College]] in 1993. She completed her master's degree in [[biophysics]] at the [[University of Rochester]] in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Irene Georgakoudi {{!}} Women in Optics {{!}} SPIE|url=https://spie.org/about-spie/advocacy/women-in-optics/women-in-optics-planner/2017-wio-planner/irene-georgakoudi|access-date=2021-01-07|website=spie.org}}</ref>

She stayed at Rochester for her doctoral studies, investigating [[photodynamic therapy]] in Professor Tom Foster's group and completing her thesis in 1999.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=The biophysicist who tries to make cancer detection a lot easier|url=https://www.ellines.com/en/achievements/24635-the-biophysicist-who-tries-to-make-cancer-detection-a-lot-easier/|access-date=2020-01-07|website=Ellines.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Georgakoudi|first1=Irene|last2=Nichols|first2=Michael G.|last3=Foster|first3=Thomas H.|date=1997|title=The Mechanism of Photofrin Photobleaching and Its Consequences for Photodynamic Dosimetry|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1751-1097.1997.tb01889.x|journal=Photochemistry and Photobiology|language=en|volume=65|issue=1|pages=135–144|doi=10.1111/j.1751-1097.1997.tb01889.x|pmid=9066293|s2cid=1253620|issn=1751-1097|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Georgakoudi was awarded several university prizes and grants during her doctoral studies, including the Graduate Alumni Fellowship, Agnes M and George Messersmith Fellowship, and the William F Neuman Award in Biophysics.<ref>{{Cite web|title=William F. Neuman and Margaret W. Neuman Scholarship Fund in Biophysics and Environmental Medicine - Awards - Biochemistry & Biophysics - University of Rochester Medical Center|url=https://www.urmc.rochester.edu/biochemistry-biophysics/awards/neuman-award.aspx|access-date=2021-01-07|website=www.urmc.rochester.edu}}</ref> She also received the Graduate Student Society Leadership Award in 1997 for her involvement in the University of Rochester's Graduate Student Society.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==

Georgakoudi's research career has focused on developing new [[Optical Spectroscopy|optical spectroscopy]] techniques for applications in [[medical imaging]] and the detection and treatment of different diseases.

She joined the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] as a postdoctoral fellow in 1999, where her research studied how [[fluorescence spectroscopy]] could improve early cancer diagnosis as an imaging tool for observing changes in [[cell growth]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2019-08-21|title=Irene Georgakoudi|url=https://engineering.tufts.edu/bme/people/faculty/irene-georgakoudi|access-date=2021-01-07|website=Department of Biomedical Engineering|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite In 2004, she joined [[Tufts University]], where she was a Professor of [[Biomedical Engineering]].<ref name=":1" /> Her research used developing optical techniques to image [[human tissue]], providing non-invasive ways to monitor changes in [[cellular metabolism]] and diagnose diseases such as diabetes, cancer, and neurodegenerative disorders.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-06-25|title=Label-free fluorescence microscopy offers early cancer detection|url=https://physicsworld.com/a/label-free-fluorescence-microscopy-offers-early-cancer-detection/|access-date=2021-01-07|website=Physics World|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Cancer metabolic pathway identified as target for therapy: Researchers identify a|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2020/07/200721132844.htm|access-date=2021-01-07|website=ScienceDaily|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Spotting Cancer at the Molecular Level|url=https://www.technologynetworks.com/cancer-research/news/spotting-cancer-at-the-molecular-level-322557|access-date=2021-01-07|website=Cancer Research from Technology Networks|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title="Biopsy Without a Knife": A New Cancer Imaging Technique|url=https://www.biospace.com/non-invasive-non-dye-imaging-method-to-spot-cancer|access-date=2021-01-07|website=BioSpace|language=en-US}}</ref>

In 2024, she joined [[Dartmouth College]], where she is Professor of Engineering and co-director of the Translational Engineering in Cancer Research Program at the [[Dartmouth Cancer Center]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-28 |title=New Faculty Embody Scholarship and Innovation {{!}} Dartmouth |url=https://home.dartmouth.edu/news/2024/10/2024-new-faculty |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=home.dartmouth.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==

* Fellow of the [[SPIE|International Society for Optics and Photonics (SPIE)]], 2020
* Fellow of the [[Optical Society of America]], 2016<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=2016 OSA Fellows|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/fellow_members/recent_fellows/2016_fellows/|access-date=2020-01-07|website=[[Optical Society of America]]}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]], 2015<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fellow Directory - AIMBE|url=https://aimbe.org/college-of-fellows/directory/|access-date=2021-01-07|language=en}}</ref>
* NSF Career Award for ''Non-invasive modalities for optical imaging of cell-matrix interactions in engineered tissues'', 2006-2011<ref>{{Cite web|title=NSF Award Search: Award#0547292 - CAREER: Non-invasive modalities for optical imaging of cell-matrix interactions in engineered tissues|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0547292|access-date=2021-01-07|website=www.nsf.gov}}</ref>
* Claflin Distinguished Scholar Award, [[Massachusetts General Hospital]], [[Harvard Medical School]], 2004<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Past Recipients of the Claflin Distinguished Scholar Award|url=https://ecor.mgh.harvard.edu/Default.aspx?node_id=552|access-date=2021-01-07|website=ecor.mgh.harvard.edu}}</ref>
